title: UN Talks on 'Killer Robots' End Without Strong Rules
subtitle: Global efforts to control autonomous weapons face delays as major military powers resist binding laws.

summary.en: International discussions at the United Nations regarding autonomous weapons have failed to produce a legally binding treaty. Despite support from over 100 countries, the need for total agreement allowed major powers to block stricter rules. These weapons, which use artificial intelligence to choose targets, are already being used in conflicts worldwide. Humanitarian groups warn that allowing machines to make life-or-death decisions is a dangerous moral line. The new agreement only provides a two-year window for further, potentially optional, discussions.
summary.zh: 聯合國針對自動化武器的國際討論未能產生具法律約束力的條約。儘管獲得超過一百個國家的支持，但由於需要完全共識，導致強權國家得以阻撓更嚴格的規範。這些利用人工智慧選擇目標的武器，已在世界各地的衝突中使用。人道主義團體警告，讓機器做出攸關生死的決定是一條危險的道德紅線。新的協議僅提供了兩年的窗口期，進行後續可能僅具選擇性的討論。

paragraphs.en: International efforts to create new rules for autonomous weapons—often called 'killer robots'—have ended without a strong agreement. After a week of intense meetings at the United Nations in Geneva, diplomats failed to pass a legally binding treaty. Instead, they reached a weak compromise that leaves the future of these technologies uncertain.
paragraphs.zh: 國際間為制定自動化武器（常被稱為「殺人機器人」）新規則所做的努力，在沒有達成強力共識的情況下告終。在聯合國（United Nations）於日內瓦進行為期一週的密集會議後，外交官們未能通過一項具法律約束力的條約。相反地，他們達成了一項軟弱的妥協，使得這些技術的未來充滿不確定性。

paragraphs.en: The talks, held under the UN’s Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons (CCW), were meant to address the growing use of artificial intelligence in warfare. These weapons can identify and attack targets with little or no human help. While more than 100 countries supported a strict, legally binding law to control these systems, the CCW requires all 128 member states to agree unanimously. This high requirement meant that a few powerful nations could stop the majority from moving forward.
paragraphs.zh: 這些在聯合國《特定傳統武器公約》（Convention on Certain Conventional Weapons，簡稱 CCW）架構下進行的會談，旨在解決人工智慧在戰爭中日益增加的使用問題。這些武器幾乎或完全不需要人類協助，即可識別並攻擊目標。儘管有超過一百個國家支持制定嚴格且具法律約束力的法律來管制這些系統，但該公約要求所有一百二十八個成員國必須一致同意。這項高門檻意味著少數強權國家就能阻止多數國家推動進程。

paragraphs.en: According to The Guardian, Russia used stalling tactics to block the process. Meanwhile, other major military powers, including the United States, were also hesitant to accept strict rules. The US suggested a five-year period for discussing optional guidelines, which many delegates felt was a way to delay real action. By 5 a.m. on the final day, the group settled on a compromise: countries will have two years to suggest regulations that may or may not be legally binding.
paragraphs.zh: 根據《衛報》（The Guardian）報導，俄羅斯採取拖延戰術來阻礙進程。與此同時，包括美國在內的其他主要軍事強權，對於接受嚴格規範也持保留態度。美國提議給予五年時間討論選擇性的指導方針，許多代表認為這只是拖延實質行動的手段。在最後一天的清晨五點，各方達成了一項妥協：各國將有兩年時間提出可能具備、也可能不具備法律約束力的規範。

paragraphs.en: Humanitarian organizations expressed deep disappointment with the result. The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), which protects the rules of war, had urged nations to create binding laws within one year. Georgia Hinds, a legal adviser for the ICRC, explained that there is a fundamental ethical problem with letting an algorithm—a set of computer instructions—make life-or-death decisions. She described this as a 'moral red line' that humanity should not cross.
paragraphs.zh: 人道主義組織對此結果深感失望。致力於維護戰爭規則的紅十字國際委員會（International Committee of the Red Cross，簡稱 ICRC）曾敦促各國在一年內制定具約束力的法律。紅十字國際委員會的法律顧問喬治亞·海因茲（Georgia Hinds）解釋說，讓演算法（即一套電腦指令）做出攸關生死的決定，存在根本性的倫理問題。她將此描述為人類不應跨越的「道德紅線」。

paragraphs.en: The urgency of this issue is clear from current conflicts. According to NPR, drones and AI-assisted weapons are already being used in places like Ukraine, Sudan, and Gaza. In Sudan, the UN reported that drones were responsible for 80% of civilian deaths this year. Furthermore, investigative reports cited by The Guardian indicate that the US military has used AI-enabled systems to carry out tens of thousands of strikes, with the goal of making 1,000 AI-assisted targeting decisions every hour.
paragraphs.zh: 從當前的衝突中，可以清楚看出此議題的急迫性。根據美國公共廣播電台（NPR）報導，無人機與人工智慧輔助武器已在烏克蘭、蘇丹與加薩等地使用。在蘇丹，聯合國報告指出，今年有八成的平民死亡是由無人機造成。此外，《衛報》引述的調查報告顯示，美軍已使用人工智慧系統執行數萬次打擊，目標是每小時做出一千次人工智慧輔助的鎖定決策。

paragraphs.en: Critics argue that the world is moving too slowly. Max Tegmark, chair of the Future of Life Institute, noted that world leaders failed to meet the moment. He warned that these weapons are already here, yet states have spent 14 years just talking about them. Anna Hehir, an expert in military AI governance, added that these systems are becoming easier to get. Unlike nuclear weapons, which are difficult to build or buy, autonomous drones can be created or purchased by many different groups, including criminal organizations.
paragraphs.zh: 批評者認為全球行動過於緩慢。「生命未來研究所」（Future of Life Institute）主席麥克斯·泰格馬克（Max Tegmark）指出，世界領袖未能把握時機。他警告說，這些武器已經出現，但各國卻花了十四年僅僅是在討論它們。軍事人工智慧治理專家安娜·赫希爾（Anna Hehir）補充說，這些系統正變得越來越容易取得。與難以製造或購買的核子武器不同，自動化無人機可以由包括犯罪組織在內的許多不同團體製造或購買。

paragraphs.en: The failure to reach an agreement highlights a long-standing problem with the CCW. Because it requires total consensus, it has not passed any new laws regulating weapons in the past 30 years. Some diplomats feel there is simply no political will to control these weapons, even as the technology advances rapidly. One European diplomat told The Guardian that the effort shown was not equal to the urgency of the situation.
paragraphs.zh: 未能達成協議凸顯了《特定傳統武器公約》長期存在的問題。由於該公約要求完全共識，過去三十年來未能通過任何規範武器的新法律。一些外交官認為，即便技術進步神速，各國也缺乏管制這些武器的政治意願。一位歐洲外交官告訴《衛報》，所展現出的努力與局勢的急迫性並不相稱。

paragraphs.en: As the world waits for the next two years of discussions, the technology behind these weapons will likely continue to improve. Many experts fear that without clear, international rules, these systems will spread further and become harder to control. While some negotiators argued that the agreement was better than nothing, many others believe it is a 'nothing burger'—a term used to describe something that seems important but has no real substance. For now, the question of who—or what—should be allowed to make the decision to kill remains an open and dangerous challenge for the international community.
paragraphs.zh: 隨著世界等待接下來兩年的討論，這些武器背後的技術很可能會持續精進。許多專家擔心，若沒有明確的國際規則，這些系統將進一步擴散並變得更難以控制。儘管一些談判代表認為有協議總比沒有好，但許多人認為這只是「空洞的承諾」——這個詞用來形容看似重要卻毫無實質內容的事物。目前，誰（或什麼）應該被允許做出殺戮決定的問題，對國際社會而言，仍然是一個懸而未決且危險的挑戰。

keyTerms.definitionEn: Delaying or obstructing a process to prevent progress.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（攤位），這裡作動詞的現在分詞，形容拖延戰術。文中：According to The Guardian, Russia used stalling tactics to block the process.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To stop something from happening or moving forward.
keyTerms.noteZh: 常見作名詞（街區、積木），這裡作動詞用。文中：According to The Guardian, Russia used stalling tactics to block the process.

keyTerms.definitionEn: To act effectively in a difficult or important situation.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 採取適當行動以應對當下的重要時刻。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是一個慣用語，字面意思容易理解，但實際是指展現出與情勢相符的領導力或行動力。文中：Max Tegmark, chair of the Future of Life Institute, noted that world leaders failed to meet the moment.

keyTerms.definitionEn: Something that is expected to be important but turns out to have no real value or substance.
keyTerms.definitionZh: 名不符實的事物、空洞無物的東西。
keyTerms.noteZh: 這是一個非正式的俚語，形容看似重要但實際上毫無意義的結果。文中：While some negotiators argued that the agreement was better than nothing, many others believe it is a 'nothing burger'—a term used to describe something that seems important but has no real substance.

quiz.question: What was the final outcome of the UN meetings regarding autonomous weapons?

options.A: A strict, legally binding treaty was signed by all 128 member states.
options.B: A compromise was reached to discuss potential regulations over the next two years.
options.C: The UN decided to ban the use of AI-assisted drones in active conflict zones.
options.D: The US and Russia agreed to a five-year period of voluntary guidelines.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 B。文章第三段明確指出，會議最後達成了一個妥協方案（compromise），即各國將有兩年的時間來提出可能具有法律約束力或不具約束力的法規。選項 A 錯誤，因為會議最終未能達成強有力的協議。選項 C 錯誤，文中並未提到有任何禁令產生。選項 D 錯誤，雖然美國曾建議五年的討論期，但最終協議的時間表是兩年，且該建議並未被完全採納為最終決議。

quiz.question: Based on the text, why is the proliferation of autonomous weapons considered more dangerous than that of nuclear weapons?

options.A: Autonomous weapons are more powerful and cause more civilian deaths than nuclear bombs.
options.B: Nuclear weapons are strictly regulated by the CCW, while autonomous weapons are not.
options.C: Autonomous weapons are more accessible and easier to acquire than nuclear technology.
options.D: The UN has already lost control over the development of autonomous weapon algorithms.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。根據第六段 Anna Hehir 的說法，核武器因為製造或購買困難，其擴散受到限制；相反地，自主無人機可以被許多團體（包括犯罪組織）輕易製造或購買，這暗示了其取得門檻較低，因此更難管控。選項 A 無法由文中推斷出兩者的威力比較。選項 B 錯誤，文中並未提到核武器受 CCW 管制。選項 D 過度推論，文中僅提到缺乏法規，並未說 UN 已失去對演算法的控制權。

quiz.question: In the final paragraph, what does the author mean by calling the agreement a 'nothing burger'?

options.A: It is a deal that lacks any significant impact or real substance.
options.B: It is a cheap and quick solution to a very expensive problem.
options.C: It is a temporary agreement that will be replaced by something better.
options.D: It is a controversial decision that upset many different groups.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 A。文中括號內解釋了 'nothing burger' 是用來形容「看似重要但實際上毫無實質內容」的事物。這對應到文章描述該協議對解決自主武器問題幫助有限的情況。選項 B 錯誤，文中並未提及成本問題。選項 C 錯誤，文中並未保證未來會有更好的替代方案。選項 D 雖然提到人們感到失望，但 'nothing burger' 強調的是「空洞、無效」，而非單純的「具爭議性」。

quiz.question: What is the central message of the article regarding autonomous weapons?

options.A: The UN has successfully established a framework to monitor AI usage in warfare.
options.B: Technological advancement in AI is moving too fast for military leaders to understand.
options.C: International consensus on autonomous weapons is difficult to achieve, leaving a dangerous regulatory gap.
options.D: Humanitarian organizations are the only groups concerned about the ethics of killer robots.

quiz.explanationZh: 正確答案為 C。全文的核心在於探討國際社會在規範自主武器上的失敗，由於 CCW 的一致同意原則以及政治意願不足，導致無法達成有效協議，進而造成監管真空（regulatory gap），這也是文章不斷強調的危險挑戰。選項 A 與事實相反。選項 B 雖然提到技術進步快，但並非文章主旨。選項 D 錯誤，文中提到許多外交官與專家也對此感到擔憂，不只是人道組織。
